terms.definition: AWS's block storage service that provides persistent, network-attached storage volumes for EC2 instances. Works like a virtual hard drive.
terms.example: Like the hard drive in your laptop — stores your OS, files, and data, but lives in the cloud and can be detached and reattached.

terms.definition: Adding new, separate resources alongside existing ones to increase total capacity. In EBS, this means attaching a new volume to the EC2 instance.
terms.example: Instead of replacing your 1TB hard drive with a 2TB drive, you plug in a second 1TB external drive alongside it.

terms.definition: Increasing the size or performance of an existing resource. In EBS, this means resizing the existing volume to a larger size.
terms.example: Replacing your 8GB EBS volume with a 20GB volume — same disk, just bigger.

terms.definition: Linux command (list block devices) that shows all disks and partitions attached to the system, their sizes, and where they are mounted.
terms.example: Running lsblk shows nvme0n1 (8GB, root) and nvme1n1 (12GB, not mounted) — helping you see both old and new disks.

terms.definition: Linux command (make file system) that formats a raw disk and creates a file system structure (like XFS or EXT4) so the OS can store and retrieve files.
terms.example: sudo mkfs -t xfs /dev/nvme1n1 — formats the new 12GB volume as XFS, preparing it for use.

terms.definition: A directory in the Linux file system tree where a disk is attached, making its contents accessible at that path.
terms.example: Mounting /dev/nvme1n1 to /data means all files on that disk appear inside the /data folder.

terms.definition: File System Table — a Linux configuration file that lists which disks should be automatically mounted when the system boots.
terms.example: Adding your EBS volume's UUID to /etc/fstab ensures it's auto-mounted to /data every time the EC2 reboots.

terms.definition: A permanent, unique identifier assigned to each formatted disk or partition. More reliable than device names (like nvme1n1) which can change after reboots.
terms.example: UUID=a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 — this always refers to the same disk, even if the device name changes.

terms.definition: Linux command (block ID) that displays the UUID and file system type of a block device. Used to get the UUID for adding to /etc/fstab.
terms.example: sudo blkid /dev/nvme1n1 returns UUID='...' TYPE='xfs' — giving you the UUID needed for fstab.

terms.definition: An /etc/fstab mount option that tells Linux to continue booting even if the specified disk is not available, preventing boot failures.
terms.example: Without nofail, detaching an EBS volume while its fstab entry remains can cause the EC2 to get stuck in a boot loop.

terms.definition: A point-in-time backup of an EBS volume stored in Amazon S3 (AWS-managed). Snapshots are incremental — only changed blocks are stored after the first.
terms.example: Like pressing 'Save' on your game progress — if something goes wrong, you can restore to exactly where you were when you saved.

terms.definition: A backup strategy where only the data that has changed since the last backup is stored, rather than copying everything again each time.
terms.example: Google Photos uploading only your 5 new photos instead of re-uploading all 200 existing ones every day.

terms.definition: The ability to restore data to the exact state it was in at a specific moment in time using a backup taken at that moment.
terms.example: If you took a snapshot Monday and data was accidentally deleted Tuesday, you can restore the Monday snapshot to get your data back.

terms.definition: Older AWS EBS SSD volume type where IOPS automatically scale with volume size at 3 IOPS per GB, with a maximum of 16,000 IOPS.
terms.example: A 500GB GP2 volume automatically gets 1,500 IOPS. You cannot change this independently.

terms.definition: Current-generation AWS EBS SSD volume type with a baseline of 3,000 IOPS regardless of size, configurable up to 16,000 IOPS and 1,000 MiB/s throughput independently.
terms.example: A 10GB GP3 volume can still have 10,000 IOPS configured — you control IOPS and throughput independently of storage size.

terms.definition: High-performance EBS SSD volume types designed for I/O-intensive workloads like databases, offering up to 64,000 IOPS (io1) or 256,000 IOPS (io2 Block Express).
terms.example: Large Oracle or SAP HANA databases requiring sub-millisecond consistent latency use io2 Block Express.

terms.definition: EBS HDD volume type optimized for large, sequential I/O workloads (big data, log processing). Cannot be used as a boot volume.
terms.example: Storing and processing server log files that are written sequentially and read in large batches.

terms.definition: A high-performance journaling file system commonly used in Amazon Linux 2023 and Red Hat-based Linux distributions. Supports large files and volumes.
terms.example: Amazon Linux 2023 uses XFS as its default file system for EBS root volumes.

terms.definition: A widely used, mature Linux file system known for its reliability and compatibility. Handles snapshot restores and dirty shutdowns more gracefully than XFS in some scenarios.
terms.example: Ubuntu Linux typically uses EXT4. EXT4 is more forgiving when mounting a restored snapshot on a different EC2 instance.

terms.definition: A launchable template that contains an operating system, application software, and one or more EBS snapshots. Used to launch new EC2 instances.
terms.example: Like a master copy of a game disc — you can use one AMI to spin up 100 identical EC2 instances at once.

terms.definition: AWS service that automates the creation, retention, and deletion of EBS snapshots and AMI-based backups on a user-defined schedule.
terms.example: Configure DLM to take daily snapshots of all production volumes and keep the last 14 days, automatically deleting older ones.

terms.definition: A physically separate, isolated data center within an AWS Region. EBS volumes exist within a single AZ and can only be attached to EC2 instances in the same AZ.
terms.example: ap-south-1b is one of three Availability Zones in the Mumbai region. An EBS volume created there can only attach to EC2s in ap-south-1b.
